idiom_name: ({ ok: true, value } | { ok: false, error }) with ok()/err() factories
implementation_notes: JavaScript's native failure channel is throw with try...catch, and promises reject for async failures, so a Result is a convention rather than a stdlib type. The idiomatic minimal form is a tagged object - { ok: true, value } or { ok: false, error } - created by two factory functions and consumed through the ok discriminant (or a small match helper). The shape costs nothing, survives JSON serialization and works in every runtime; what it lacks is enforcement: nothing stops a caller from reading result.value on a failure, so a lint rule or TypeScript narrowing is what makes it safe. Keep the error field a code or enum-like value rather than a message, and convert thrown errors at the boundary with a try/catch wrapper so the rest of the code stays exception-free.
pitfalls: Nothing enforces the check: r.value on a failure is undefined (or a stale branch value), so a lint rule or TypeScript narrowing carries the discipline.
Truthiness is not the test - { ok: false } is truthy - so branch on the ok field explicitly.
Async code needs a second decision: a rejected promise is not a Result, so awaited calls must be wrapped at the same boundary or the reason is lost.

variants.name: neverthrow Result / ResultAsync (library)
variants.implementation_notes: neverthrow packages the contract as classes: ok(value)/err(error) constructors, Result.isOk/isErr, map/mapErr, andThen/orElse, match for terminal handling, unwrapOr for defaults, and fromThrowable/Result.fromThrowable for converting throwing code at the boundary. ResultAsync wraps Promise<Result<T, E>> and is thenable, so map/andThen keep working across async boundaries where a bare promise rejection would erase the typed reason; the companion eslint plugin ports Rust's must-use idea by forcing every Result to be consumed through match/unwrapOr/_unsafeUnwrap. Choose the library where the error contract spans many modules and that lint enforcement is worth the dependency; the plain tagged object stays the zero-dependency form.
variants.idiom_name: Result<T, E> with ok/err, map/andThen/match and ResultAsync
pitfalls: The eslint plugin is what enforces consumption; without it a forgotten Result is as silent as any ignored return value.
_unsafeUnwrap bypasses the contract and throws; keep it for tests and proven invariants and use unwrapOr/match in production paths.
